=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:456-460 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_push_targets` drops the first positional refspec even when `--repo` supplied the remote, so the explicit push destination may never be checked.
  WHY: A push using `--repo` can fall back to checking the session checkout instead of its destination; severity disagreement: minimax_minimax-m3 rated this BLOCKER while the other reviewers rated it MAJOR, so critical reflects the highest rating.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1272-1353 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: If the structured parser returns no git invocations after the guarded-subcommand precheck matched, `_evaluate_bash` silently allows the command without checking a target.
  WHY: A guarded push or commit can bypass the merged-PR check when parsing fails; severity disagreement: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro rated this BLOCKER, google_gemini-3_8-flash and minimax_minimax-m3 rated it MAJOR, and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated it NIT, so critical reflects the highest rating.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:472-475 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The source-validation regex rejects valid Git revision expressions and falls back to checking the session checkout instead of the parsed destination.
  WHY: A push using a revision expression such as `HEAD~1:feature/merged` may not check the destination branch, allowing a push the guard should block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:466-470 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A bare `HEAD` refspec is treated as a destination branch literally named `HEAD` rather than being resolved to the branch Git will push.
  WHY: The guard queries PR status for a branch named `HEAD`, so a push from a merged branch can pass unchecked; severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, and z-ai_glm-5_2 rated this BLOCKER while openai_gpt-6-luna and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated it MAJOR, so critical reflects the highest rating.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:342-346 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The environment-assignment matcher does not recognize `NAME+=value` assignments.
  WHY: An append assignment such as `GIT_DIR+=... git push` can leave the parser pointed at the assignment instead of `git`, causing the command or its repository context to be missed.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:322-326 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `||` handling tracks the working directory incorrectly for subsequent commands.
  WHY: A `cd` on a branch that does not execute can be applied to later commands, while a valid `cd <worktree> || exit` path can lose its tracked directory, causing the guard to check the wrong checkout or fall back to it.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_shell_segments_with_operators (lines 254-265) and _push_targets (lines 420-455) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Redirection operators split shell command segments so push arguments can be detached from the parsed git invocation.
  WHY: Redirections before or after push arguments can cause the destination refspec to be ignored or trigger an unintended fallback to the session checkout.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:(diff hunk _push_targets, invocation.warning early return) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When the working directory cannot be resolved, `_push_targets` discards an explicit parseable refspec and checks the session checkout instead.
  WHY: A push to an explicit destination can be evaluated against the wrong branch, causing a false block or allowing a push that should be blocked.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “Resolve the effective repository for each guarded git command” and judge pushes by their destination branch and source commit; update §21.B to document the new behavior.
  expected_change_site: CLAUDE.md §21.B and workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md §21.B
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Neither file is changed in the PR; both still describe checking the current branch and whether the merged PR head is an ancestor of HEAD, while the hook uses the effective repository and push destination/source tip.
- requirement: "For `git push <remote> HEAD:<ref>` or `<src>:<ref>`, check the **target ref** (`<ref>`) for a merged PR with no open PR, not the local branch name. A detached HEAD pushing to an open PR's branch must be allowed."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` `_push_targets`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `_push_targets` treats a bare `HEAD` refspec without a colon as destination branch `HEAD`, so the actual destination branch is not checked; the acceptance test suite does not include bare `git push origin HEAD` from a merged checkout.
- requirement: Tests cover the acceptance criteria including edge cases for bare HEAD and revision expressions as push sources.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: New tests cover explicit source tips like `feature/x`, but none exercises bare `HEAD` as a refspec or a revision expression like `HEAD~1` as the source.
- requirement: "Keep the §21.D budget: one cached REST call per (slug, branch) pair judged."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` `_evaluate_bash` PR snapshot memoization
  confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: Memoization keys on `(slug, branch)`, not `(slug, branch, tip)`; when refspecs share a destination but push different sources, the cached pull-request result is reused for the second source's ancestry check.
- requirement: "If the directory cannot be resolved (a variable, a subshell), keep today's behaviour for that command and log a warning. Don't fail open silently."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` `_evaluate_bash`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: A `ValueError` from `shlex.shlex` makes `_guarded_git_invocations` return an empty list, so `_evaluate_bash` emits no warning and returns `0, ""` despite the guarded-subcommand precheck matching.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_push_targets`, `refspecs = positionals[1:]`) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The parser treats the first positional as the remote even when `--repo <remote>` already consumed the remote, dropping the first refspec.
  WHY: `git push --repo origin feature/x:feature/y` checks the checkout branch instead of `feature/y`, so a push to a merged branch can pass unblocked.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_evaluate_bash`, the for-invocation loop) | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: If `_shell_segments_with_operators` raises `ValueError` or the parser finds no git invocations, the loop does not run and the function returns 0.
  WHY: A shell command the structured parser cannot parse can bypass the merged-PR guard.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_push_targets`, source validation) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The source-validation regex rejects valid Git revision expressions such as `HEAD~1`, `HEAD^`, and `main@`.
  WHY: The guard falls back to checking the session checkout instead of the push destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_guarded_git_invocations`, `||` operator handling) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `conditional_cd` is set only for `&&`, not `||`.
  WHY: After `true || cd /worktree`, the parser applies the worktree path to subsequent commands although the `cd` did not execute, potentially bypassing the guard.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_push_targets`, invocation.warning early return) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When the working directory cannot be resolved, `_push_targets` discards the explicit refspec destination.
  WHY: The guard checks the session checkout branch instead of the parseable destination, causing a false block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (diff hunk `_guarded_git_invocations`, assignment-skip regex) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The assignment matcher does not recognize `NAME+=value` append assignments.
  WHY: A `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE` override can be missed, causing the repository context to be incorrect.
- Requirement: CLAUDE.md §21 describes checking "the current branch" and whether "the merged PR's head commit is an ancestor of HEAD."
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md §21.B and workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md §21.B
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff changes neither CLAUDE.md file; §21 still describes the old behavior, unlike the guard's updated docstring.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
